comment: Reference of the CTE export for SQLite, read by the tests of the TypeScript serialiser (web/src/components/result/__tests__/cte.spec.ts), which must write expected-sqlite.sql byte for byte with the lexical settings of a SQLite session (double quotes for the names, no backslash escapes), and by crates/connectors/tests/cte.rs, which loads the rows into a table of the declared types, reads them back as the connector gives them, with the families of the columns, then runs expected-sqlite.sql, which must give back the same names and cells, with the families of read_back. SQLite has no typed literal of a date or a time: these values are strings; bytes are written in hexadecimal and come back as a BLOB; a NUMERIC column keeps 12.50 as the REAL 12.5 and -3.00 as the INTEGER -3.
